study.question: Does the observed action-content advantage in the two target-match summary rows survive removing the additional item-embedding gradient introduced by the item-content replacement, and does this optimization sensitivity depend on task-specific versus shared residual routing? This is conditional attribution within the strongest inherited family; historical actions remain in direct pooling, ordinal summaries and released task masks.
study.hypothesis: Observation, frozen before new code: g1-r0034 observed minus item_duplicate click AUC is 0.0025194215263166786 with task routing and 0.0030543329673365927 with shared routing. All have 32129765 parameters at one frozen seed. Round 35 retaining only raw versus only scaled observed action gives 0.6658683269047254 versus 0.6658657278996007 with task routing, and 0.6636240164932762 versus 0.6642230835900453 with shared routing. The corresponding raw-by-scaled finite-difference interactions are -0.0017646153793682284 and -0.0014038338374697812. These are descriptive validation observations, not significance estimates. Proposed mechanism: observed action coordinates carry predictive content beyond existing item summaries; their replacement deficit should persist when only the extra backward path into item summaries is removed. Alternative mechanism: redundant item-coordinate gradients under the fixed single-pass optimizer partly cause the loss and apparent routing interaction. A forward-identical attached/blocked contrast tests that alternative directly.

study.proposed_difference: Add one architecture selector match_replacement_gradient=attached|blocked. After the unchanged FP32 sum/sqrt(F) calculation, blocked applies duplicate.detach() before the unchanged cast and selected-row torch.where. The ordinary item_summaries coordinates are never detached. Attached executes the inherited arithmetic unchanged. Cross this selector with task/shared routing in a four-cell design, both match-action rows replaced in every submitted cell. Preserve supported observed and mixed-content identity/bridge endpoints. Before host training: finite four-task train/eval forward and backward in FP32 and frozen BF16; exact learned state keys/shapes/initial values and RNG/buffer parity across cells. At fixed parameters (initial and a nonzero residual-bank state) attached versus blocked within each routing must have identical predictions, summaries, Dice moments and running state. Attached endpoints must match the materialized history_g1_r0035_match_raw_observed_task.py with match_action_content=item_duplicate and the same routing, including predictions, dense/sparse gradients, RNG, buffers and one frozen optimizer step; compare resulting full-run receipts with g1-r0034-match_itemdup_task/shared as a descriptive bridge, not an independent repetition. At the helper, selected rows 0/4 must be independent of incoming action coordinates in both modes, with identical values; derivative to item_summaries through the replacement is 1/sqrt(F) in attached mode and zero in blocked mode (before dtype effects); ordinal rows 1/2/3 are identities. End-to-end, only the added replacement contribution to the primary item-embedding gradient may change at fixed state. Dense model gradients, direct action/context gradients and auxiliary ownership should agree within predeclared numerical tolerances; inspect sparse indices, coalesced values and None versus zero semantics. Normal item-summary/pool/scorer gradients must remain live. Test empty/singleton/partial/full/noncontiguous masks, excluded IDs, current-target-action perturbations and invalid-history-ID perturbations with fixed legal masks; preserve missing/malformed task-mask rejection. Replacement must precede original availability and summary-family gates so disabled rows cannot be restored. Bound FP32/BF16 errors before examining validation scores. Abort attribution if another information, gradient, state or mask path changes. These are required host checks, not completed local tests.
predictions: At a fixed full parameter state, attached and blocked replacement cells within a routing have identical complete forward values and state updates; only the intended primary replacement-to-item-embedding derivative differs. Measure the helper Jacobian at nonzero residual-bank weights, because zero final initialization can hide the intervention.

If historical action content has utility robust to this replacement-gradient alternative, blocked item_duplicate will remain below the matching observed-content references g1-r0034-match_observed_task (0.6662444304756373) and g1-r0034-match_observed_shared (0.6647487996065942). No new scores are predicted as established facts.

falsifiers: Blocked replacement closes or reverses the observed-minus-duplicate deficit in either routing: reject robust content attribution in that routing and investigate optimizer/gradient geometry before a stronger action-content claim.
No reproducible attached-versus-blocked effect weakens the specific redundant-item-gradient explanation; it does not prove all optimization confounds absent.
Failure of attached-source parity, forward identity, gradient localization, mask/ownership checks or measured parameter equality invalidates this attribution experiment regardless of favorable AUC.
A routing interaction that fails paired repetition, or changes direction across admissible seeds, cannot establish task-conditioning dependence. This phase offers no new-seed execution override.

No result here establishes novelty, production point-in-time feedback utility, total history-action value, or action-label causality. Neither source gains nor this one-seed intervention identify those claims.
alternative_explanations: The action encoding, label construction and official_offline delayed feedback policy may supply benchmark-specific predictive associations; frozen masks themselves retain action-derived membership.

Different information rank, variance, summary scale, readout conditioning, optimization and representation learning remain despite identical parameter count and fixed-state forward values in the gradient comparison. Detaching replacement does not freeze item embeddings; ordinary paths still update them.
Task/shared routing has equal instantiated and executed bank capacity but differs in effective specialization and gradient sharing; it is not a proof of capacity equivalence.
Raw/scaled summaries are partly redundant; the negative finite differences in round35 may arise from substitutability or fixed-recipe optimization, not causal biological-style interactions.

Prior trajectories show zero/context action replacement losses (round24), scorer-only loss versus value-only near preservation (round25), partial pool/summary recovery (round26), mixed alignment/removal paths (round27-33), and item-content replacement deficits (round34-35). None of these source branches exceeds the unchanged joint incumbent. Same-seed reproduced endpoints are parity checks, not independent mechanism replications.
